newsitem.title: INDIA: India says 96/97 export growth below expectations.
newsitem.headline: India says 96/97 export growth below expectations.

text.p: India's Commerce Ministry said on Monday that export growth in fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) was not "as high as we would have liked it to be owing to a number of international and domestic factors".
"In value terms, exports have increased from $18.5 billion in 1992/93 to around $33-34 billion in 1996/97, a near-doubling of export values in five years," the ministry said in a statement.
Between April 1996 and January 1997, merchandise exports totalled $27.07 billion, up 6.19 percent from $25.49 billion over the same 10-month period from April 1995 to January 1996.
In 1995/96, exports were valued at $31.83 billion, 21.38 percent higher than in 1994/95 when they totalled $26.22 billion.
